headline: Agents can reach the simulator; humans still define success
synthesis: The expanded library makes the next constraint clearer: native agents are gaining real Mac runners, simulator control, structured UI inspection, screenshots, video, and release automation, but access is not the same as judgment. Anam Hira, onevcat, Loupe, and Sunday Swift show increasingly complete verification loops; Matt Corey demonstrates how an automated screenshot run can still finish with every iPad capture wrong. Oleh Veheria, Donny Wals, Chris Eidhof, and SWE-Bench Mobile define the human boundary around architecture, concurrency, product value, and evaluation. The most durable pattern is therefore explicit acceptance criteria, machine-readable evidence, narrow autonomy, and a named human owner for decisions the toolchain cannot prove.
